cases.rationale: A turns finite capacity into a concrete, memorable place-register device while keeping the ledger quiet, object-first, and explicitly non-coercive. Its exact palette, field order, hostile states, focus recovery, and candid limitations are unusually actionable. B is sound and complete, but the availability rail is largely a conventional action column and its system is less visually specific.

B provides the stronger subject-specific system: a checkpoint ticket that progressively converts unresolved rows into confirmed booking facts. It ties exact visual tokens and responsive structure to the brief, covers ambiguous timezone, slot exhaustion, facilitator change, conflict, and connection loss, and treats retention as conditional rather than promised. A is coherent and usable but more closely resembles generic step-form guidance.

tier1_failures: invented context: submission failure is specified to preserve entered content without conditioning that behavior on confirmed implementation or policy

cases.rationale: A makes provenance the visual identity through a continuous Trail Ledger that spans entry, review, tracking, correction, and recovery. It is concrete about responsive transformation, high-contrast behavior, upload failure, interruption, and uncertainty, and it explicitly refuses to promise persistence. B has a coherent provenance spine and good semantics, but unconditionally prescribing preserved input crosses from direction into an unsupported system guarantee and its visual treatment is less fully resolved.

B develops the decision bench into a concrete equipment-specific system: exact workbench tokens, a constraint spine, reversible paper-tab markers, and explicit evidence-to-confirmation ordering. Its hostile-state set, breakpoints, keyboard model, concurrency caution, and conditional draft-retention language make the operational coverage especially realistic. A is strong and faithful, but its decision tray and split-pane treatment are more generic and its failure and concurrency coverage is thinner.

limitations: Grading was based solely on the supplied blind text. No rendered artifacts, interaction prototypes, implementation evidence, or source brief beyond the content embedded in the pairs were available, so visual and accessibility judgments assess the specificity and credibility of the proposed direction rather than verified execution.
